title: A bivalent molecular glue linking lysine acetyltransferases to oncogene-induced cell death.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Downloaded and opened: one RNA-seq file (GSM8747531, kallisto transcript abundance, 227,912 transcript rows x 5 columns: target_id/length/eff_length/est_counts/tpm); the BCL6 CUT&RUN peak file GSM9364532 (5,237 peaks, standard 10-column narrowPeak); the p300 ChIP peak file after 2 h TCIP3 (3,159 peaks) versus the DMSO p300 peak file (8 KB, near-empty); the GSE287543 series matrix, which shows the full design (39 samples = 5 DLBCL cell lines, one compound TCIP3 at 1 nM vs DMSO, timepoints 0.5/1/2/4 h in SUDHL5 and 4 h in the other four lines, 3 biological replicates); GEO file manifests for all three series (GSE287542 ChIP-seq 32 samples / 2.9 GB of bigWig coverage tracks, GSE287543 RNA-seq 39 samples / 104 MB, GSE313235 CUT&RUN 4 samples / 324 MB); the PRIDE file list for PXD059919 (8 files, 753 GB total: four raw mass-spectrometry zips of 55-344 GB each plus four DIA-NN 'SEARCH' result tables); and one of those search tables (1073_IP_FLAG_SEARCH.parquet, 14 MB, 132,721 rows x 67 columns of peptide-precursor-level data with UniProt IDs, gene symbols and MaxLFQ intensities, no fold-change or hit column). Also confirmed PDB entry 9MZA resolves in the RCSB (Protein Data Bank) API. Confirmed the supplementary tables are NOT retrievable: Europe PMC refuses them ('Article with id PMC13592201 is not open access'), and the three PMC supplement paths return 404, 403 and an HTML stub.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: The 859-cell-line PRISM viability profiling of TCIP3/TCIP1/CDK-TCIP1 (Figure S12D) and the BCL6-level vs area-under-the-dose-response-curve correlation (Pearson R = -0.83 across 9 lines) are read from the text only; no PRISM table is deposited. Contents of Table S2 (cell-line variants), Table S3 (immunoprecipitation mass-spectrometry hits and whole-proteome changes) and Table S4 (transcription-factor enrichment) are known only from their captions. Compound structures live in Methods S1/Data S1 inside the non-downloadable supplement; compounds themselves are 'available upon request with a materials transfer agreement'.

a1_downloadable.note: Processed genomics downloads cleanly and anonymously from GEO (I fetched three files). But the only tabular supplements (Tables S2-S4) are unreachable because the article is not open access, the mass-spectrometry raw data is 753 GB, and the SUDHL5 whole-genome data sits behind a reviewer-token BioProject link. Pass on the genomics only.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: FAIL. Nothing deposited contains a prediction target as a column. Every candidate label must be built: gene-level TCIP3 response needs transcript-to-gene collapsing plus a differential-expression test across 39 files; proteomics response needs collapsing 132,721 peptide precursors to protein groups and then a statistical test; chromatin features need summarising 2.9 GB of bigWig coverage over gene loci.

a3_inputs_present.note: Inputs are present as identifiers that resolve locally: Ensembl transcript IDs in the RNA files, UniProt accessions and gene symbols in the proteomics table, genomic coordinates (GRCh38) in the peak files. Verified in the files.

a4_units_stated.note: Units are explicit: transcripts per million and estimated counts in the RNA files; signal fold-enrichment and -log10 p/q values in narrowPeak; MaxLFQ normalised intensities in the proteomics parquet. Verified in the files.

a5_enough_rows.note: FAIL on independent units. The experiment is 39 RNA-seq samples spanning 13 conditions in 5 cell lines, one compound at one dose, plus 32 ChIP-seq and 4 CUT&RUN samples. Transcript rows (227,912) and peptide rows (132,721) are measurements of the same few samples, not independent examples; far under the ~1,500-row bar once counted properly.

a6_fits_laptop.working_set: ~0.5 GB if only RNA abundance tables and narrowPeak files are used; ~3.3 GB if the bigWig coverage tracks are included
a6_fits_laptop.note: Would fit a 16 GB laptop with per-file streaming; verified from the GEO manifests and the files I downloaded.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: GEO sample counts (39 RNA-seq, 32 ChIP-seq, 4 CUT&RUN) match the deposited design; could not cross-check the supplementary tables because they are not downloadable.

a8_label_provenance.note: All measurements are physical (RNA sequencing, chromatin immunoprecipitation/CUT&RUN, mass spectrometry, X-ray crystallography), not another model's output. A8 is not the problem here; A2 and A5 are.

existing_models.name: MiTCP (Molecule-induced Transcriptional Change Predictor), Briefings in Bioinformatics 2025
existing_models.score_and_split: Reported to predict compound-induced changes in 978 'landmark' genes; exact metric and split not retrieved (search abstract only)

existing_models.name: TranSiGen, a self-supervised generative model of chemical-induced transcriptional profiles (Nature Communications 2024)
existing_models.score_and_split: Reconstructs compound-induced expression profiles from basal cell expression plus molecular structure; numbers not retrieved

existing_models.name: DeepTernary / GlueMap / ET-PROTACs (2025 molecular-glue and PROTAC ternary-complex predictors)
existing_models.score_and_split: Ternary-complex structure prediction benchmarks on curated sets such as TernaryDB; numbers not retrieved

backbone.name: Enformer or AlphaGenome (DNA sequence to chromatin/expression) would be the natural backbone for a gene-response task; ESM-2 (protein language model) for a proteomics task
backbone.hardware: CPU feasible for a frozen-embedding head, but moot given the label problem
backbone.licence: Not assessed; project rejected at Part A

integration.partner_dataset: DepMap (gene dependency and omics for ~1,100 cancer cell lines) joinable on cell-line name, and ChIP-Atlas for blood-lineage transcription-factor binding
integration.join_key: cell line name (5 lines only) / GRCh38 genomic coordinates
integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: Which chromatin features at a repressed gene decide whether chemically forced recruitment of the acetyltransferase p300 switches it on - but with one compound in five cell lines there are not enough held-out groups to answer it.

controls.positive_control: The model should recover that known BCL6 target genes with strong BCL6 binding are the ones induced (the paper's own central finding), plus a trivially learnable target such as gene length from the coverage features.
controls.negative_control: Shuffle the per-gene response labels and confirm collapse to the global mean; ablate the BCL6 occupancy feature block.
controls.external_validation: The sibling TCIP datasets GSE211282 (BRD4-recruiting TCIP1, 85 samples) and GSE290893-5 (EWSR1::FLI1 rewiring in Ewing sarcoma) exist and are public, so a cross-compound transfer test is possible - the one genuinely attractive feature of this family of datasets.

honest_claim_h3: A model built on this paper's data could only claim: within five BCL6-driven diffuse large B cell lymphoma lines treated with one molecule at one dose for up to four hours, baseline chromatin state ranks which repressed genes become induced - a claim about one compound in one disease, with no held-out compound, dose or tissue to test it on.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use a gene's baseline chromatin state to predict whether a bivalent drug switches that gene on.
plain_idea.train_on: For each human gene, features summarising baseline binding of the repressor BCL6 and the acetyltransferase p300 plus histone acetylation signal around the gene; roughly 20,000 genes, but all derived from 5 lymphoma cell lines and 39 RNA-sequencing samples (counts verified in the files).
plain_idea.predict: The change in that gene's messenger RNA level after 4 hours of 1 nM TCIP3, measured by RNA sequencing (deposited as kallisto transcript-abundance tables) and turned into a fold change by a differential-expression test the analyst has to run.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Chemists designing transcriptional chemical inducers of proximity would like to know in advance which repressed genes a new molecule will activate; even a failed model would quantify how much of the response is explained by baseline chromatin alone.

more_or_better_data.why: The deposited data is 39 RNA-sequencing samples from one compound in five cell lines. LINCS L1000 holds compound-induced expression profiles for tens of thousands of compound-cell-line pairs, which is what TranSiGen and MiTCP were built on.

confidence_score.why: Three biological replicates per condition do let you estimate measurement noise per gene, but with 13 conditions there is no way to calibrate confidence across compounds, doses or cell types.

models_beatable.why: The named transcriptional-response models (TranSiGen 2024, MiTCP 2025) are recent and trained on far larger perturbation corpora; nothing here could out-train them, and their reported splits were not retrieved so no honest comparison is set up.

guaranteed_improvement.why: No existing model can be run as a baseline on this task, the label is not even measured the same way (RNA sequencing fold change here versus L1000 bead-based profiles there), and there is no shared evaluation split.

label_elsewhere.sources: LINCS L1000 (compound-induced transcriptional profiles; known public resource) and the sibling public TCIP series GSE211282, GSE290893, GSE290894, GSE290895, which I found by searching GEO for TCIP/BCL6 and confirmed exist with sample counts.
label_elsewhere.join_key: cell line name plus compound identifier (InChIKey where structures are published); Ensembl gene ID for the response vector
label_elsewhere.why: Compound-induced expression change is measured for very many compounds elsewhere, so the right project in this space would start from LINCS L1000 and use papers like this one as a held-out test case, not as the training set.

ml_idea: The project considered was: predict, per gene, the transcriptional response to the molecular glue TCIP3 from baseline chromatin features (BCL6 CUT&RUN occupancy, p300 ChIP-seq, histone acetylation) using a frozen DNA-sequence backbone plus a head, with transfer tested on the public BRD4-recruiting (GSE211282) and EWSR1::FLI1 (GSE290895) TCIP datasets. It dies because the label does not exist as a column anywhere and the experiment contains only 13 conditions in 5 cell lines with a single compound and dose.

effort.compute_note: Estimated, not timed: ~0.5 GB for the 39 RNA abundance tables plus narrowPeak files (I downloaded three of them), ~2.9 GB more if the bigWig coverage tracks are summarised; the 30 hours is the differential-expression plus coverage-aggregation pipeline needed to create any label at all.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Count the independent experimental units before anything else: open the GSE287543 series matrix (5 KB) and see 39 samples = 13 conditions, 5 cell lines, 1 compound, 1 dose. That kills it in one minute.

verdict_reason: Fails A2 and A5. This is a mechanism-and-chemistry paper, not a dataset: the deposited genomics (39 RNA-seq, 32 ChIP-seq, 4 CUT&RUN samples) and proteomics (peptide-level search tables) contain no prediction-target column, so any label would have to be constructed by running differential expression, and the real sample size is 13 conditions in 5 cell lines with one compound at one dose. The tabular supplements that might have held a label table are unreachable because the article is not open access, and the 859-cell-line PRISM sensitivity data the paper describes was never deposited.
